title: A Guide to Delhi's Haunted Hotspots, With Eric Chopra
excerpt: A good share of the eerie atmosphere also comes courtesy of the Aravallis and the Delhi Ridge. Here's why...
content:
Few cities in India carry a reputation for being haunted like Delhi. It’s actually not too much of a stretch if you think about it – almost every neighbourhood in the city’s lined with centuries-old tombs, crumbling ruins, and remnants of the seven ancient cities that preceded what we know as Delhi today. But a good share of the eerie atmosphere also comes courtesy of the Aravallis and the Delhi Ridge. 

The Aravallis (incidentally one of the world's oldest fold-mountain systems) are lush with tangled branches, sparse foliage, and ancient ruins –  some modest, some monumental, and all dating to different centuries. They’re also one of author, podcaster and public historian Eric Chopra’s central motivations behind his book, Ghosted: Delhi's Haunted Monuments. 

Read further: The Aravallis have a lot more on offer than spooky stories. Check out Time Out Delhi’s guide on the best things to get up to there. 

Back in college at St Stephen's, Delhi University, he’d roam the fringes of the Aravalli forests in search of hidden monuments. Each spot often came with something else attached: spooky stories of ghosts, djinns and spirits, from the tale of a headless angrez to rumours of melting bodies.

One of the city's finest qualities – feel free to disagree – is that you rarely have to work hard to get people talking. Wait a few minutes and chances are you'll be handed a bizarre anecdote, a local legend or a popular myth. The city carries a bag full of them. Many of Eric's ghost stories began exactly that way.

The author's visits to these places are hardly occasional, even now. Many of them also feature on Itihasology, the history platform he jointly runs with Kudrat Singh, a history scholar.

The hauntings were simply too good to ignore. So we invited Eric to lead us on a walk through the fringes of the Aravallis, where history, folklore and ghost stories overlap each other. Here are three spots we ventured with him.
